That is not impossibility for any budget, provider or model.

model_artifacts_at_the_pinned_revision.licence: CC BY-NC 4.0, research only; incompatible with any commercial or trading use
model_artifacts_at_the_pinned_revision.why_all_four_adapters: the repository's own remote code calls snapshot_download(allow_patterns=['adapters/*']) at load time whenever the model path is not a local directory, so an offline load needs the whole adapter set materialised

model_wrapper_version_declaration.option_a: the published row's evaluator version plus our own reconstruction of the model wrapper
model_wrapper_version_declaration.option_b: the first evaluator version whose registry names the model and pins this very revision; its draw and scorer are source-identical to the published row's for this task
model_wrapper_version_declaration.what: the registry of the version that produced the published row does not name the selected model at all; the first release that names it is later. So a reproduction must declare which of two configurations it ran, and may not print either as though it were the other.

third_pinned_environment.pip_cache_caveat: the cache is large enough to plausibly already hold the installed torch/transformers blobs, so a same-version install may need no network at all - NOT verified, because verifying it means attempting a resolve

tier_1_if_the_installed_transformers_tor.evidence_for_this_tier: every symbol the repository's remote code imports - Qwen3Model, Qwen3Config, PreTrainedModel and snapshot_download - resolves under the installed transformers line, checked by import on the admissible host with no weights loaded. That is necessary, not sufficient: the code has not been RUN, because running it needs the weights.

tier_2_if_it_does_not.note: the declared toolchain on the model card is transformers 4.57.0 / torch 2.8.0 / sentence-transformers 5.1.2; the admissible host carries a newer line

third_pinned_environment.transitive_closure: NOT_RESOLVED; resolving it is itself a network act and belongs to the same single request
third_pinned_environment.why_not_reuse: both retained environments are pinned to a Laya SDK version, and installing into either would mutate an environment a published reproduction depends on. The native route needs its own environment.

dependency_ledger.the_exact_unfulfilled_dependency: an approved acquisition of 1,369,721,378 bytes of model artifacts at the pinned revision, plus a third pinned Python 3.13 environment carrying datasets, mteb, peft, scikit-learn, sentence-transformers (16,228,123 bytes of direct wheels at tier 1, transitive closure unresolved), together with an explicit decision to execute the repository's remote code.

deterministic_recipe.evaluator_model: sklearn LogisticRegression(n_jobs=-1, max_iter=100), random_state set to the task seed
deterministic_recipe.indices_are_the_mirror_indices: the contract records the mirror's text sequence as identical to the authors' in file order on both splits, so an index computed on the registered CSV is the same row the published evaluator drew
deterministic_recipe.label_id_mapping_is_irrelevant_here: the greedy counter buckets by label equality only, and category -> mirror id is a bijection, so the selected indices do not depend on which of the three recorded label orders is used
deterministic_recipe.what_is_still_missing_after_this: only the embeddings: the draws, the probe, the seed, the scorer and the rows are fixed, and the encoder is the one unfulfilled dependency

forced_metric_identities.premise: every class has exactly the same test support
forced_metric_identities.what_it_does_not_license: MACRO_F1 and WEIGHTED_F1 remain different declared families and a comparison between them still refuses by name even where they coincide numerically; accuracy against macro-F1 refuses likewise
forced_metric_identities.what_the_identity_adds: the equality of the two keys is FORCED by the balanced support, and the published artifact shows exactly the three identities the balance predicts, which corroborates that its population is our population
forced_metric_identities.what_the_published_f1_is: macro-F1 by the pinned source's own definition - `f1` is computed with average='macro' and `f1_weighted` with average='weighted' - so the published 0.913809 is a MACRO_F1 comparison target on its definition, not on this coincidence
forced_metric_identities.why: a weighted average with equal weights IS the unweighted average, and accuracy is the support-weighted mean of per-class recall

mirror_substitution_carried_forward_not_.why_it_matters: a naive sorted() map mislabels most of the 77 classes; the ids are carried from the contract and not re-derived here
